correctness.rationale: All pairwise graph distances ≤p-1 except antipodal pairs, hence a cross-polytope sphere. Rotation is the signed coordinate shift with polynomial λ^p+1, -1 line plus primitive unit complex weights. Hemisphere modulo rotations yields mapping cone of degree-two lens covering; van Kampen gives π1=C2. The C_p quotient is the universal double cover ΣL_p; Hurewicz gives π2=C_p. Standard integral lens homology and transfer show f_* injective on odd torsion and ×2 on top free homology, giving exact projective-space homology. The proof covers all odd primes; finite verifier checks p=5,7,11 and cannot substitute for the universal argument.

value.rationale: The full-rotation quotient is canonical for regular even polygons at their last noncontractible Rips stage. It produces infinitely many spaces indistinguishable from real projective spaces by integral homology but with nonzero prime-order π2, increasing through all odd primes. The mapping-cone identification is structural and allows explicit nontrivial homotopy detection, beyond a routine counting exercise or a previously known source sphere.
